why: The student rewrites b as the maths-style range !(5 < n < 10), which does not compile in Java, and keeps the !( ) instead of applying De Morgan, so the answer uses a rule that goes against Java.

concepts.quote: You could write b as !(5 < n < 10).
concepts.why: It is not a De Morgan rewrite: the negation is not moved inside, the comparisons are not flipped and && is not turned into ||. The correct form is n <= 5 || n >= 10.
The answer makes no claim about variables.
The answer says nothing about how &&, || or ! work.
The answer makes no claim about short-circuit evaluation.
The answer makes no claim about string concatenation.
The answer makes no claim about assignment.
The answer makes no claim about arithmetic operators.
The answer makes no general claim about expressions.
It writes the range as a chained comparison the way maths does. In Java 5 < n gives a boolean, so 5 < n < 10 does not compile (ChainedComparison).
